requirements.description: Daily Datastream firm-security data to construct closing quoted spreads, daily returns/zero returns, quarterly price impact, return variability, market value, and daily share turnover. USD trading volume can be constructed as share Volume × close_usd; market value can be built from close_usd × numshrs.

required_coverage.population: International firm securities in up to 35 IFRS treatment countries (24 EU) and 21 benchmark countries. For the supporting trading-cost fit, the source reports 699,517 quarterly estimates, exceeding the 561,590 factor-regression observations; therefore inputs must include the broader support-fit population before factor complete cases and later baseline screens. The exact firm/security roster and local coverage are unconfirmed.
required_coverage.detail: Baseline outcomes and supporting models run in 2001Q1–2009Q4. The three firm controls are lagged four calendar quarters, so the earliest raw control quarter is 2000Q1; the union is 2000Q1–2009Q4. Window arithmetic: anchor 2001–2009 plus 12-month lookback gives the conservative year envelope 2000–2009.

variable_coverage.construction: For each firm security and trading day compute (ask−bid)/the quote midpoint from closing bid/ask, then take the quarterly median and natural log. Datastream is the primary source; the paper supplements Bloomberg spreads for Czech Republic, Luxembourg, Slovakia, and Slovenia and CRSP spreads for U.S. firms in unspecified early years.

Code the post-mandate IFRS observation for firms in the Table 1 EU countries whose IFRS mandate was bundled with substantive enforcement changes; use actual Worldscope fiscal-period-end dates, the quarter-after-first-fiscal-year-end rule, ITEM7536 for IFRS reporting, and the dated Datastream–Worldscope firm link.

Code the post-mandate IFRS observation for the remaining EU countries without bundled enforcement changes, using Table 1 country coding, the firm’s actual Worldscope fiscal-period-end date, the following-calendar-quarter switch, ITEM7536, and the dated firm link.
Code post-mandate IFRS observations for non-EU IFRS adoption countries using Table 1 membership/date, actual firm fiscal-year ends, Worldscope ITEM7536, and the dated security-to-firm link.
At quarter end compute close_usd×numshrs/1,000,000 for market value in US$ millions, lag four calendar quarters, then take the natural log.
For each trading day compute US$ turnover as share Volume×close_usd divided by same-day market value close_usd×numshrs; take the quarter median at t−4, then take the natural log.
Compute the standard deviation of daily Datastream returns within quarter t−4, then take the natural log.

design_coverage.reason: The selected Table 3 column (6) reports OLS and does not specify observation weights; no additional weight data are required for this baseline.
The selected Panel A fit is OLS; no additional estimation input beyond the listed model variables is specified.

implementation_issues.description: The sample screen excludes firms with average market value below US$5 million, but the paper does not state the averaging period or whether the average is daily, quarterly, or over a different window. This prevents an exact reconstruction of the retained firm population.

Datastream security/company IDs and the dated Worldscope crosswalk are available as candidate fields, but no coverage confirmation or firm-country/fiscal-record join has been verified for the 2000–2009 sample. The paper’s country unit also needs to be matched to the Datastream company-country field.

Table 1 supplies country groups and mandate dates, and the paper defines activation using the quarter after each firm’s first fiscal-year end after the mandate. Coding those categories is feasible from the paper, but mapping them to a firm’s country and Worldscope reporting-standard code remains unresolved.

The available Datastream and Worldscope probes are current local snapshots, while the article was published in 2013. Historical values, security links, and coverage may differ from the authors’ extraction vintage.

review_notes: The paper’s Table 3 column (6) is the selected three-quarter-year-trends baseline; no later robustness specification or WLS sensitivity model is added.
The Datastream spread series is supplemented by Bloomberg in four smaller EU markets and CRSP for early U.S. years; those are mandatory source-specific inputs for the paper’s reported sample.

variable_coverage.construction: Estimate the quarterly firm-level total round-trip trading-cost proxy from daily security returns and the equal-weighted local-market return series using the cited log-likelihood system; impose the stated ≥24 daily returns, ≥20% nonzero-return, and ≥1 basis-point estimate filters. This is a generated support measure from two jointly required raw series.
Use the daily equal-weighted local market index return series paired to each firm-day as the aggregate-market-return input to the quarterly trading-cost system.

For each firm-quarter form the four proxy inputs: median daily closing spread using the quote midpoint; zero returns divided by all potential trading days; median daily absolute return/USD volume excluding zero-return days; and the nested quarterly total-trading-cost estimate. Extract the first/only factor with eigenvalue>1 and compute ln(score+1). The cost-estimation output and the other proxies are all required inputs.

Code the post-mandate IFRS observation for firms in the Table 1 EU countries with bundled enforcement changes, using actual firm fiscal-year ends, the following-calendar-quarter switch, ITEM7536, and the dated firm link.
Code post-mandate IFRS observations for the remaining EU countries without bundled enforcement changes, using Table 1 country coding, actual firm fiscal-year ends, ITEM7536, and the dated firm link.
Code post-mandate IFRS observations for non-EU adoption countries using Table 1 country/date coding, actual fiscal-year ends, ITEM7536, and the dated firm link.
At quarter end compute close_usd×numshrs/1,000,000, lag four calendar quarters, and take the natural log.
Compute daily US$ share turnover as Volume×close_usd divided by same-day close_usd×numshrs, take the quarter median at t−4, and take the natural log.
Compute the within-quarter standard deviation of daily Datastream returns at t−4 and take the natural log.

design_coverage.reason: The selected Table 3 column (6) reports OLS and does not specify observation weights; no additional weight data are required for this baseline.

implementation_issues.description: The sample screen excludes firms with average market value below US$5 million, but the paper does not state the averaging period or whether the average is daily, quarterly, or over a different window. This prevents an exact reconstruction of the retained firm population.

Datastream security/company IDs and the dated Worldscope crosswalk are available as candidate fields, but no coverage confirmation or firm-country/fiscal-record join has been verified for the 2000–2009 sample. The paper’s country unit also needs to be matched to the Datastream company-country field.

Table 1 supplies country groups and mandate dates, and the paper defines activation using the quarter after each firm’s first fiscal-year end after the mandate. Coding those categories is feasible from the paper, but mapping them to a firm’s country and Worldscope reporting-standard code remains unresolved.

The available Datastream and Worldscope probes are current local snapshots, while the article was published in 2013. Historical values, security links, and coverage may differ from the authors’ extraction vintage.

The total-trading-cost proxy is extracted by a quarterly log-likelihood system from daily security and equal-weighted local index returns, with 24-return, 20%-nonzero, and 1-basis-point filters. The article does not print the likelihood system or all parameter/return conventions; it points to Lesmond et al. (1999) and an appendix in Daske et al. (2008), so that implementation must be confirmed before the supporting fit can be reproduced exactly.

The liquidity-factor rule specifies factor analysis and the first/only eigenvalue above one, but does not specify the extraction method, input standardization, score normalization/sign, or missing-input handling. These choices affect the exact factor score passed through ln(score+1).

The paper requires equal-weighted local market index returns but does not identify the exact index series or country-market construction. The local Datastream index RI and constituent/weight tables are candidate inputs; neither verifies the paper’s equal-weighted index definition or all required country/date coverage.

The zero-return denominator is all potential trading days per quarter. The Datastream date field does not establish whether every potential exchange session is represented when a firm has no valid return; the exchange calendar/observation rule is unresolved.

The paper says CRSP adds U.S. bid/ask data in the early sample years but does not state the cutoff years or exact CRSP product/quote-time convention. The local CRSP daily file has candidate BID/ASK fields, but the exact required dates and Datastream-to-CRSP firm match remain unverified.

review_notes: Table 2 reports 699,517 total-trading-cost observations versus 561,590 liquidity-factor observations. The support input population is therefore assessed before the smaller factor complete-case/regression sample; do not restrict support inputs to the final factor N.
The paper requires Bloomberg spreads for four smaller EU markets and CRSP spreads for early-year U.S. observations in addition to Datastream. The exact CRSP early-year cutoff is not printed.
The Datastream index series and constituent table were inspected as candidate local-market inputs; fields alone do not verify the equal-weighted series used by the authors.

evidence.quote: Our sample period starts in the first quarter of 2001 and ends in the fourth quarter of 2009.
evidence.description: Baseline firm-quarter calendar sample.

evidence.quote: The sample comprises up to 35 IFRS treatment countries, of which 24 belong to the EU, and 21 benchmark countries.
evidence.description: International treatment and benchmark population.

evidence.quote: We exclude firms in IFRS countries that follow U.S. GAAP and firms with a U.S. cross-listing
evidence.description: Sample exclusions based on accounting standards and cross-listing.

evidence.quote: we eliminate firms trading on unregulated EU markets
evidence.description: Unregulated EU market exclusion.

evidence.quote: drop very small firms with average market values below US$ 5 million, and require benchmark countries to have at least 20 firms.
evidence.description: Average market value and benchmark-country sample filters.

evidence.quote: Panel A also lists the dates when IFRS reporting became mandatory, the calendar quarter during which the substantive change in enforcement took place
evidence.description: Country-level mandate and enforcement dates reported in Table 1.

evidence.quote: the EU countries that switched to IFRS and, at the same time, implemented substantive enforcement changes (IFRSEU_ENF)
evidence.description: Country group definition for the Table 3 treatment variable.

evidence.quote: IFRS is a binary indicator variable for firm-quarters with IFRS reporting that takes on the value of ‘1’ beginning in the calendar quarter following the first fiscal-year end after IFRS became mandatory.
evidence.description: Treatment date follows the first fiscal year end under the mandate, then the following calendar quarter.

evidence.quote: We identify firms that do not follow IFRS after the mandate based on the “accounting standards followed” field in Worldscope (field 07536).
evidence.description: Worldscope accounting-standards field cited by authors.

evidence.quote: We include country-, Campbell (1996) industry-, and quarter-year-fixed effects
evidence.description: Table 3 fixed effects.

evidence.quote: we draw statistical inferences based on two-way clustered standard errors by country and calendar quarter.
evidence.description: Two-way standard-error clustering.

evidence.quote: The Bid-Ask Spread is the quarterly median quoted spread
evidence.description: Quarterly median of daily quoted spreads.

evidence.quote: difference between the bid and ask price divided by the mid-point and measured at the end of each trading day
evidence.description: Daily closing quoted percentage spread definition.

evidence.quote: Zero Returns is the proportion of trading days with zero daily stock returns out of all potential trading days per quarter.
evidence.description: Zero-return numerator and potential-trading-day denominator.

evidence.quote:
Price Impact is the quarterly median of the Amihud (2002) illiquidity measure (i.e., daily absolute stock
return divided by US$ trading volume).
evidence.description: Price-impact measure.

evidence.quote: we omit zero-return days from the computation of the quarterly medians
evidence.description: Price-impact exclusion for zero-return days.

evidence.quote: Total Trading Costs are an estimate of the total round trip transaction costs
evidence.description: Estimated total transaction-cost proxy.

evidence.quote: based on a quarterly time-series regression of daily stock returns on the aggregate market returns (Lesmond et al., 1999).
evidence.description: Source description of quarterly return-cost estimation.

evidence.quote: we require at least 24 daily returns and 20% of the daily returns to be different from zero per firm-quarter
evidence.description: Support-fit observation thresholds.

evidence.quote: we eliminate estimates below one basis point
evidence.description: Support-fit estimated-cost filter.

evidence.quote: Total Trading Costst 699,517
evidence.description: Table 2 reports a broader total-trading-cost count than the factor count.

evidence.quote: factor scores from the first (and only) factor with an Eigenvalue greater than one
evidence.description: Factor-score selection rule.

evidence.quote: the Liquidity Factor equal to the factor scores extracted from the four individual measures bid-ask spreads, zero returns, price impact, and total trading costs using factor analysis
evidence.description: Factor outcome inputs.

evidence.quote: Market Value is stock price times the number of shares outstanding (in US$ million) measured at the end of the quarter.
evidence.description: Market-value control formula and timing.

evidence.quote: Share Turnover is the quarterly median of the daily turnover
evidence.description: Share-turnover quarterly aggregation.

evidence.quote: US$ trading volume divided by the market value at the end of each trading day
evidence.description: Share-turnover daily denominator.

evidence.quote: We compute Return Variability as the standard deviation of daily stock returns in a given quarter.
evidence.description: Return-variability quarterly aggregation.

evidence.quote: We estimate the liquidity regressions in a log-linear form using the natural logarithm of the dependent variables and the control variables, and lag the control variables by four quarters.
evidence.description: Log transformations and four-quarter firm-control lag.

evidence.quote: Because the Liquidity Factor can assume negative values we add one to the raw score before computing the natural logarithm.
evidence.description: Liquidity Factor log-plus-one transformation.

evidence.quote: We truncate all continuous variables at the first and 99th percentile.
evidence.description: Continuous-variable truncation.

evidence.quote: Price and volume data are from Datastream.
evidence.description: Primary price and volume source.

evidence.quote: Our primary source of bid-ask spread data is Datastream.
evidence.description: Primary bid-ask source.

evidence.quote: we complement this data with spreads from Bloomberg
evidence.description: Bloomberg spread supplement for smaller EU markets.

evidence.quote: For U.S. firms, we add spread data from CRSP because Datastream does not have this data in the early years of our sample period.
evidence.description: CRSP spread supplement for early-year U.S. observations; exact early-year cutoff is not stated.

evidence.quote: The table reports OLS coefficient estimates
evidence.description: Selected Table 3 baseline estimator; Table 3 column (6) does not report weights.
